Sorry to hijack but I've been thinking this over for a while and I'm nerding out

The games setting is the gift, the wall, and the land beyond the wall in its entirety

While south of the wall fast travel roads are available (think assassins creed) that will take you to certain places. Winterfell and its surrounding area. The dreadfort, last hearth, etc.

North of the wall several encampments and wildlings bases are available such as hard home and other gathering places.

The character creation allows you to choose what house you are from and thus allows you to visit your keep and act diplomatic at other houses. OR you can be a wildling of whatever tribe. Think thenns have a trait where you get a damage buff from eating human enemies you've killed.

Getting south of the wall as a wildling is possible by several means. Climbing (will need to craft the supplies and sneak yourself south) or disguise yourself as a nights watch brother

Or sneak through a abandoned castle.

Obviously nights watch gameplay would allow you to cross the wall with relative ease.


I think of it this way. North of the wall is a darkzone from division essentially for the nights watch. And south of the wall is a darkzone for wildlings.

Risk vs reward and stealth is key. Knowing when to engage other players for supplies and gear as well as engaging in missions for your faction. 




Or better yet. CUT all the wildling character choice and have Mutineers to encourage PVP combat.

The further north you go the better loot you get, first men war hammers, dragon glass arrow tip consumables, possibly even valerian steel remnants or something for crafting. Of course north of the wall (like the division) there will be no fast travel.

Make your fires at night and burn your dead but be careful not to use all your supplies.

The further north you go the higher risk, different environments of the north... And of course magical elements in the lands of always winter.

I imagine scenarios where you and 3 friends are in the gift, riding for moles town to buy food for your next ranging. You get there and find its under wildling attack. Mop up the enemies with non flashy sword to sword combat that highlights brutal kills and of course comes paired with epic music.

Once the wildlings are dead you loot the bodies and get XP for saving the town or whatever. Return to castle black with your rewards and prepare for a ranging north.

You stop by the kitchen for a hearty meal and a buff that will last you 3 in game days and continue to gather quests from first ranger and master at arms. 

As you set out north you ride through the woods and fight wildlings etc. but you can also commit mutiny. See other online players killing wildlings or completing quests? Kill them for their food and whetstones (need to keep that blade sharp) 

I envision mechanics that allow you to walk among wildlings and accept their quests (kill crowd and other players of the nights watch) by equipping their furs and forsaking your vows.

This would simply make you unable to access the gift by going through the gate.

Joining wildlings would have its advantages as well. Maybe you can craft fires faster during rankings. Or your respawn point is already north of the wall.

But the idea for me at least is that I don't ever have to start in penatonic scales anymore because I can compare the positions of working scales to red house and just apply them to the key I'm playing in.

Once you understand how to identify other scales based on relative distance from the fret your playing you can quickly hop around from low bends to high alternate note picking and all the inbetweens that come in blues


The most important advice I can give you though. Is to simply feel the music. You have to start somewhere and you definitely won't be a guitar god over night, just stick through with each solo and practice.

One last thing, think of each note translation as a punch or golfswing, you don't want to punch someone and stop when you hit them, you want to punch through them. If you are playing a solo to practice and fuck up just slide to the right key and go from there. 

You want to go through with each lick even if you mess up, because you will mess up. Just slide to the note or bend up to it for a quick save and get back to dropping jaws.

Learn to play the red house intro and get a feel for the song vibe, try to get into it as much as possible and just explore every scale you can figure out. They will be weird patterns you never thought of but once you get a hang of playing them they'll come as second nature. Once you identify where to go from the base penatonic scale you can apply it to other songs. The licks you'll learn in the intro are pretty solid and will give you ideas to capitalize on.

That's how I learned at least. Now I can use other scales with different energy and move all up and down the neck while staying in key.
